name: Zara's braces and the bone around her teeth

parameters.label: Weeks wearing braces
parameters.explain: Teeth move slowly through bone; whole treatments usually take one to two years.

parameters.label: Hours a day wearing her bands
parameters.explain: The bone only keeps remodelling while the push keeps going; short spells of force let it settle back.

parameters.label: How hard the braces push
parameters.explain: Test the 'pull harder, go faster' idea: heavy force moves teeth only a little faster and makes them much sorer.

parameters.label: Gap to close
parameters.explain: A bigger gap takes longer to close; once it's closed, the tooth stops.

parameters.label: Days since tightening
parameters.explain: Teeth are sore for a few days after the braces are fitted or adjusted, then settle; adjustments come every 6–8 weeks.

overlay.caption: steady push → bone taken down on one side, built up on the other → tooth moves

explain.summary: Zara's braces push her tooth gently and steadily. On the side being pushed, bone-clearing cells take bone away; on the other side, bone-building cells lay new bone down. So the tooth moves through her jaw a fraction of a millimetre a week. A fresh push after tightening makes teeth sore and a bit loose for a few days. Without the steady push, the bone stops remodelling.
rules: Tooth movement grows steadily with the weeks she wears her braces.
Bone is taken down on the pushed side and built on the other side.
Fewer hours of force a day means slower movement; very short spells do almost nothing.
Heavier force moves the tooth only a little faster but makes it much sorer.
Soreness and looseness peak right after tightening and fade within days.

source.fact: Teeth move because bone is resorbed by osteoclasts on the pushed (compression) side and built by osteoblasts on the tension side.
The first reaction to a new push is inflammation, including pain, that usually lasts a few days.
Teeth may be sore for a few days after braces are fitted; braces are adjusted every 6 to 8 weeks and usually stay on for 1 to 2 years.
Heavier forces tended to increase the rate of tooth movement but brought unwanted side effects; initial movement benefits from light forces.
Orthodontic treatment typically takes over 18 months.

choice.what: The tooth moves about 0.155 mm a week (about two-thirds of a millimetre a month) at full wear
choice.why: Closes Zara's 4 mm gap in about six months, as clue 3 says, and fits treatments lasting over a year. We could not open a source giving a typical rate in millimetres.

choice.what: Less than about 6 hours of force a day moves the tooth almost not at all; full speed needs about 22 hours
choice.why: Shows clue 4 (no bands, no progress). The real cut-off varies; the 6 and 22 hours are our estimate.

choice.what: Heavy force is 15% faster than medium and light is 15% slower
choice.why: The study found heavier forces somewhat faster; the exact size here is our estimate.

choice.what: Soreness halves every 2 days after tightening
choice.why: Matches 'sore for a few days' and clue 1 (fades in two or three days).

illustrative: Zara's 4 mm gap, her 22 hours a day and the 0–10 soreness scale are made up for a fictional story.

citations.title: Selective modulation of the bone remodeling regulatory system through orthodontic tooth movement: a review (Danz & Degen)
citations.supports: Orthodontic tooth movement works by bone resorption by osteoclasts on the compression side and bone formation by osteoblasts on the tension side; patients first feel an inflammatory reaction, including pain, that usually lasts a few days.

citations.title: Orthodontics
citations.supports: Fixed braces usually stay in place for 1 to 2 years; teeth may be sore for a few days after braces are fitted; the orthodontist adjusts them every 6 to 8 weeks; contact them if teeth are painful for more than a few days.

citations.title: Rate of tooth movement under heavy and light continuous orthodontic forces (Yee et al., American Journal of Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopedics) — abstract record
citations.supports: Over 12 weeks, heavier forces (300 g) tended to increase the rate and amount of canine retraction compared with light forces (50 g), but with unwanted side effects; initial tooth movement would benefit from light forces.

citations.title: Surgical procedures for accelerating orthodontic treatment
citations.supports: Orthodontic treatment typically takes over 18 months to complete.

does: Shows a tooth moving steadily through the jaw while a gentle force is applied
Shows bone around the tooth being taken down on one side and built up on the other
Shows movement slowing when the force acts for fewer hours a day
doesnt: Measure any real person's teeth — the numbers are illustrative teaching values
Include how braces are planned or adjusted
Describe anything beyond mild, normal tenderness
limits.text: This is a simplified learning model. Real people vary with age, fitness and health. The numbers are illustrative, not measurements of any real person.
limits.wellbeing: Sharp pain, a broken wire or a sore in your mouth that won't heal is a reason to tell an adult.
